t: What Read Uncommitted Internals Is All About
title: What Read Uncommitted Internals Is All About
description: The weakest isolation: dirty reads allowed, almost never what you want.. This database covers Read Uncommitted Internals with full records: definitions, key facts, working procedures, and runnable demo programs, arranged on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. Isolation levels define which anomalies are possible.
definition: Read Uncommitted Internals — The weakest isolation: dirty reads allowed, almost never what you want.
key_points: Isolation levels define which anomalies are possible.
Read-uncommitted allows dirty reads; almost never use it.
Read-committed is the default; each statement sees committed data.
Repeatable-read gives transaction snapshots; phantoms vary by engine.

description: What it allows. Transactions read uncommitted changes — dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantoms are all possible. It's essentially 'no isolation' for reads. Rarely the right choice.

title: Dirty read mechanics
description: Dirty read mechanics. No shared locks on read; writers' uncommitted rows are visible. A rollback makes the read retroactively wrong. This is the anomaly that defines the level.
definition: Dirty read mechanics — No shared locks on read; writers' uncommitted rows are visible.
key_points: No shared locks on read; writers' uncommitted rows are visible.
A rollback makes the read retroactively wrong.
This is the anomaly that defines the level.
Write skew is SI's famous anomaly; know the doctors-on-call example.
Lost updates are prevented by row locking at read-committed+.

title: Postgres behavior

Non-repeatable reads are allowed at read-committed by design.
First-committer-wins prevents lost updates under SI.

Postgres's repeatable-read is snapshot isolation.
